response.sql: SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, AVG(CASE WHEN l.DNA <> '' AND l.DNA NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.]*' THEN CAST(l.DNA AS REAL) END) AS avg_dna, AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS avg_alb_minus_tp FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.`T-CHO` >= 180 GROUP BY p.SEX;

assumptions.assumption: Laboratory.DNA is TEXT, so only plain decimal strings (digits and dots) count as values. Blank strings, NULLs, and entries such as '<8' are treated as missing and excluded from the DNA average.

Each laboratory record is tested on its own against T-CHO >= 180, with no per-patient aggregation. Records with NULL T-CHO are excluded. Records without a matching Patient row are dropped by the inner join.
NULL and empty-string SEX values each form their own group, because GROUP BY keeps them separate. The sex column shows NULL for a missing value and '' for a blank one.

alternatives.interpretation: Values written with a leading comparison sign, such as '<8', are read as their numeric bound (8) and included in the DNA average instead of being treated as missing.
alternatives.sql: SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, AVG(CASE WHEN LTRIM(l.DNA, '<>') <> '' AND LTRIM(l.DNA, '<>') NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.]*' THEN CAST(LTRIM(l.DNA, '<>') AS REAL) END) AS avg_dna, AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS avg_alb_minus_tp FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.`T-CHO` >= 180 GROUP BY p.SEX;
